intro: Ten stories from the last day, rewritten in plain British English. Tap any word you don't know.

items.title: Two Italians killed in Kuwait drone attack
items.text: Two Italian defence technicians were killed in a drone attack on Kuwait on Thursday. Kuwaiti and Italian authorities have blamed Iran. The men worked for Rheinmetall and were maintaining detection equipment for Kuwait's air defence systems. A Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national were also injured. Iran has denied responsibility, and an armed forces spokesman called the attack a false flag operation. Italy's foreign minister said the drone was made in Iran. Iran's foreign minister has offered to work with Kuwait and Italy to find out where it came from.

gloss.defence technician: a skilled worker who looks after military equipment
gloss.blame: to say that someone is responsible for something bad
gloss.deny responsibility: to say that you did not do something
gloss.false flag operation: an attack made to look as if another side did it
gloss.spokesman: a person who speaks officially for a group

items.title: Trump says he urged Putin to pull back
items.text: President Trump said on Thursday that he had urged Vladimir Putin to end military aggression across Europe. The two men met in Shenzhen last week. Mr Trump did not say which Russian actions he wanted to stop. His comments came after Russian missiles and drones entered Polish airspace during attacks on Ukraine earlier this week. Mr Trump and NATO's Secretary General, Mark Rutte, issued a joint statement asking Russia not to widen the conflict. The Kremlin has blamed Kyiv for trying to expand the war.

gloss.pull back: to stop doing something or move away from it
gloss.widen: to make something larger or wider
gloss.blame: to say that someone is responsible for something bad

items.title: Britain contacts 100,000 former troops
items.text: Britain has reportedly contacted about 100,000 former military personnel to find out whether they could return to service in a war. The Ministry of Defence has invited members of its Strategic Reserve to volunteer for training, including NATO exercises in spring 2027. Former personnel were asked to update their contact details and give information about their jobs and skills. Officials say taking part is voluntary and that no immediate mobilisation is planned. The regular army is approaching 73,000 people, its smallest size for more than 200 years.

gloss.personnel: the people who work in an organisation, such as the army
gloss.reserve: a group of trained people who can be called on when needed
gloss.volunteer: to offer to do something without being forced
gloss.voluntary: done by choice, not because you must
gloss.mobilisation: preparing and organising troops for war

items.title: Real Madrid thrash PSV in Champions League
items.text: Real Madrid beat PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday. Kylian Mbappe scored twice, and Jude Bellingham, Federico Valverde and Vinicius Junior each scored once. In other games, Arsenal drew 1-1 at home to Borussia Dortmund, and Manchester City drew 2-2 with Napoli. Galatasaray beat Aston Villa 1-0. Real Madrid now lead the league phase table. Arsenal and City each dropped points.

gloss.thrash: to beat a team very easily
gloss.league phase: the first stage of the Champions League, where every team plays several matches
gloss.draw: to finish a match with the same score for both teams
gloss.drop points: to fail to win a match

items.title: Spain beat Austria to reach Davis Cup semis
items.text: Spain beat Austria 2-0 in the Davis Cup quarter-finals in Bologna on Thursday. Daniel Merida won the first match 6-4, 6-4 against Joel Schwaerzler. Rafael Jodar then beat Jurij Rodionov 2-6, 6-0, 6-1, winning 12 of the last 13 games. Carlos Alcaraz did not play and was on standby for the doubles. Spain will now face Great Britain in the semi-final on Saturday.

gloss.quarter-final: a match in the last eight of a competition
gloss.doubles: a tennis match with two players on each side
gloss.semi-final: a match in the last four of a competition
gloss.comeback: a recovery after playing badly or losing

items.title: New York bans AI chatbot toys for five years
items.text: New York's governor, Kathy Hochul, has signed a law banning the making and selling of toys that use AI chatbots. The ban will last for five years and starts in February. The law shows growing worry about how children use artificial intelligence. The governor signed the bill this week.

gloss.chatbot: a computer program that talks with people in writing or speech
gloss.artificial intelligence: computer systems that can do tasks that usually need human thinking
gloss.state: a region with its own government inside a country

items.title: Congo Ebola outbreak passes 12,000 cases
items.text: Congo's government said on Thursday that its Ebola outbreak has reached 12,021 confirmed cases and 5,904 deaths. The outbreak began in May in Ituri province and has spread to 8 of the country's 26 provinces. It is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment. Fighting between government forces and rebels has blocked response teams from some communities. A WHO official said it has also disrupted contact tracing.

gloss.outbreak: a sudden rise in cases of a disease
gloss.strain: a particular type of a virus
gloss.rebel: a person who fights against the government
gloss.contact tracing: finding people who may have caught a disease from an infected person
gloss.disrupt: to interrupt something so that it cannot work normally

items.title: V&A to open punk and pop exhibition
items.text: The V&A in London will open a new exhibition called Punk to Pop in March 2027. It will show around 300 objects from 1972 to 1985. The display will be at the museum's South Kensington site. It covers a period that started in the early 1970s and ended in the mid-1980s. The announcement was made on Wednesday.

gloss.exhibition: a public display of art or objects
gloss.object: a thing that can be seen or touched, such as clothing or a poster
gloss.organiser: a person who plans an event
gloss.site: a place where something is located
gloss.announcement: a public statement about something new

items.title: Europe picks De Cos as next ECB president
items.text: European leaders have chosen Pablo Hernandez de Cos to lead the European Central Bank when Christine Lagarde steps down on 7 February. He is a former governor of Spain's central bank. If confirmed, he will be the first Spaniard to hold the job. He won the support of France and Germany over the former Dutch central banker Klaas Knot. Eurozone inflation stands at 4%, double the ECB's target.

gloss.governor: the head of a central bank
gloss.central bank: the national bank that controls money supply and interest rates
gloss.inflation: the rate at which prices rise
gloss.target: a number or goal that you try to reach

items.title: GTA VI is biggest launch in PlayStation history
items.text: Sony says Grand Theft Auto VI is the biggest game launch in PlayStation history. More than 39 million players played it on PS5 between 19 and 22 November, according to Sony's own data. Players logged 683 million hours in total. Sony also said it was the first game played on 70% of new PS5 consoles. To build excitement, Sony and Rockstar offered two Vice City DualSense controllers and held a launch festival in Miami.

gloss.launch: the first release of a product to the public
gloss.log hours: to record the time spent doing something
gloss.build excitement: to make people more interested and eager
gloss.console: a device used to play video games
